title: UGC / AICTE Official Attendance & Condonation Policy
content: Under UGC and AICTE regulations, a minimum of 75% attendance in aggregate per semester is mandatory to appear in end-term examinations. Universities allow up to 10% condonation relaxation (bringing the minimum threshold to 65%) for valid medical reasons or participation in university-approved sports, NCC, or NSS events. Applications for condonation must be submitted with official medical certificates from a recognized medical officer prior to exams. Students below 65% attendance are detained and not eligible for condonation under any circumstances.

title: University Revaluation & Examination Regulations
content: Under university regulations, the revaluation fee is Rs 600 per subject for undergraduate programs. Basic rechecking (totalling errors only) costs Rs 350 per subject. Revaluation applications must be submitted online via the student portal within 15 days of result declaration. The average of two external examiners marks is treated as the final revaluation result. Submission of examination forms after the primary deadline attracts a late fee of Rs 500. The last date for exam form submission without late fee is 30/10/2026.

title: Central Library Rules & Overdue Fines
section: Section 1: Book Issue and Return Policy
content: Undergraduate students can borrow up to 3 books for a maximum duration of 14 days. Postgraduate students may borrow up to 5 books for 21 days. Overdue books attract a fine of Rs 5 per day per book. Lost books must be replaced or compensated at 3 times the current market price. Library cards are non-transferable and must be presented at the time of issue.

title: UGC Anti-Ragging Regulations and Helpline
content: Ragging in any form is a criminal offence under UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions 2009. The university follows a zero-tolerance policy. Every student and parent must submit an online anti-ragging undertaking at www.antiragging.in during admission. The institution has constituted a mandatory Anti-Ragging Committee and Anti-Ragging Squad for surprise inspections. Complaints can be reported to the 24x7 National Anti-Ragging Helpline at 1800-180-5522. Principals and registrars are held personally accountable for failure to prevent ragging. Penalties range from suspension to expulsion and FIR filing with local police.

title: Hostel and Mess Management Rules
section: Section 4: Hostel Accommodation and Mess Charges
content: Hostel accommodation is allotted on a merit-cum-means basis. Hostel fee is Rs 15000 per semester and mess charges are Rs 12000 per semester payable in advance. All hostel residents are required to join the attached mess. Individual cooking in rooms is strictly prohibited for fire safety reasons. Night-out permission requires prior written approval from the Warden. Visitors are allowed only in the common area between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM. The Mess Management Committee meets monthly to review food quality and hygiene standards.

title: UGC Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) and Grading
section: Section 5: Internal Assessment and Grading Scale
content: Under the UGC CBCS framework, internal assessment (Continuous Internal Evaluation or CIE) constitutes 25% of total marks and the end-semester examination covers the remaining 75%. Internal marks are distributed as follows: 10 marks for mid-semester test (best of two attempts), 10 marks for assignments and seminars, and 5 marks for attendance. The university follows the UGC recommended 10-point grading scale: O (Outstanding, 10 points, 90-100%), A+ (Excellent, 9 points, 80-89%), A (Very Good, 8 points, 70-79%), B+ (Good, 7 points, 60-69%), B (Above Average, 6 points, 50-59%), C (Average, 5 points, 40-49%), P (Pass, 4 points, 35-39%), F (Fail, 0 points, below 35%). SGPA and CGPA are calculated using credit-weighted grade point averages.

title: UGC Fee Refund Policy for Students
section: Section 6: Fee Refund on Cancellation or Migration
content: If a student cancels admission before the start of the academic session, the institution must refund the full fees minus a processing charge of Rs 1000. Cancellation within 15 days of the start of classes entitles a refund of 80% of fees. Cancellation between 15 and 30 days attracts a 50% refund. No refund is applicable after 30 days from the start of classes. Caution money and security deposits are fully refundable upon completion of the program or at the time of leaving the institution.

title: Student Grievance Redressal Mechanism
section: Section 7: Grievance Committee and Complaint Process
content: Every institution must constitute a Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) as per UGC guidelines. Students may file written complaints regarding academic matters, fee disputes, harassment, or administrative issues. The SGRC must acknowledge the complaint within 3 working days and resolve it within 15 working days. If the student is unsatisfied with the SGRC resolution, they may escalate the matter to the university Registrar or file an online complaint with UGC through its official grievance portal at www.ugc.gov.in. Anonymous complaints are also accepted for sensitive matters.
